name: Question 17
worked_solution:
First, we note that 

$$
F(t)=\int {F}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t=\int ⟨3(t-1)^{2},\,4{t}^{3}-1⟩\text{d}t
$$

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\int ⟨3(t-1)^{2},\,4{t}^{3}-1⟩\text{d}t & =⟨\int 3(t-1)^{2}\,\text{d}t,\int (4{t}^{3}-1)\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨{(t-1)}^{3}+{c}_{1},\,{t}^{4}-t+{c}_{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

  

The initial condition $F(1)=⟨1,\,1⟩$ gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(1)=⟨{((1)-1)}^{3}+{c}_{1},\,(1)^{4}-(1)+{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨1,\,1⟩ \\ ⟨{c}_{1},\,{c}_{2}⟩ & =⟨1,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${c}_{1}=1$ and ${c}_{2}=1.$ Consequently

$$
F(t)=⟨{(t-1)}^{3}+1,\,{t}^{4}-t+1⟩.
$$

Question 17

If F′(t)=⟨3(t−1)2,4t3−1⟩ and F(1)=⟨1,1⟩, then F(t)=

a
⟨(t−1)3+1,t4−t+1⟩
b
⟨(t−1)3+1,t55−1⟩
c
⟨t3+2,t4−2⟩
d
⟨(t−1)4+1,t44−4⟩
e
⟨t3+1,t4−t+1⟩
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we note that

F(t)=∫F′(t)dt=∫⟨3(t−1)2,4t3−1⟩dt

To integrate a vector-valued function, we integrate each component separately. So, we have

∫⟨3(t−1)2,4t3−1⟩dt=⟨∫3(t−1)2dt,∫(4t3−1)dt⟩=⟨(t−1)3+c1,t4−t+c2⟩.

The initial condition F(1)=⟨1,1⟩ gives F(1)=⟨((1)−1)3+c1,(1)4−(1)+c2⟩=⟨1,1⟩⟨c1,c2⟩=⟨1,1⟩.

Therefore, c1=1 and c2=1. Consequently F(t)=⟨(t−1)3+1,t4−t+1⟩.
